2.title: Order-book parameter prose swaps minQuantity and lotSize
2.original_evidence:
- Page text, fetched 2026-11-01 14:05 UTC: https://somnia-platform-docs.vercel.app/markets/somnia-markets/contracts
  - "getOrderBookParameters() returns tickSize, lotSize, and minQuantity in raw token units"
  - Same page: `struct OrderBookParameters { uint256 tickSize; // min price increment ... uint256 minQuantity; // min order quantity ... uint256 lotSize; // min quantity increment ... }`
- dreamDEX developer page, fetched 2026-11-01 14:02 UTC: "getOrderBookParameters() on the pool returns the raw tickSize, minQuantity and lotSize, in that order."
- Chain, block 38891340 (2026-11-01 ~14:13 UTC), raw `eth_call` words:
  - BTC-PERP 0x4181dd08E73BbCdd1Ba3E615A18f6abD941b94C0: [100000000000000000, 13000, 1000]. At 8 base decimals: tick 0.1, word 2 = 0.00013 BTC, word 3 = 0.00001 BTC.
  - SOL-PERP 0xB483ec1fb34996638677c20ab087b16F1896FA53: [10000000000000000, 100000000, 10000000]. At 9 base decimals: word 2 = 0.1 SOL, word 3 = 0.01 SOL.
- The dreamDEX market table gives "Min size" 0.00013 BTC and 0.1 SOL. That matches word 2, so word 2 is minQuantity and word 3 is lotSize. The SDK's `listPerpMarkets()` rows agree: BTC `minQuantity` "13000", `lotSize` "1000".

3.title: Trailing-24h candle statistics omit the partial first hour
3.original_evidence:
2026-11-01, nowSec 1793542130 (14:08:50 UTC), indexer head ≈ 38,886,000:

| | BTC | ETH |
|---|---|---|
| window the SDK folds | [1793458800, now] = 83,330 s (23.15 h) | 83,338 s |
| seconds dropped | 3,070 | 3,062 |
| trades dropped (51 × 60 s candles + edge fills) | 2,102 of 76,157 (−2.76 %) | 549 of 11,146 (−4.93 %) |
| quote volume dropped | 3,428,448.64 USDso of 115,859,255.34 (−2.95 %) | 1,778,297.17 of 31,453,994.41 (−5.65 %) |
| `openPrice24h` SDK / first fill ≥ now−24h | 77,457.50 / 77,572.50 (Δ 115.00) | 2,244.45 / 2,248.57 (Δ 4.12) |

High and low were unaffected in this run, but they can be too, whenever the extreme falls in the dropped slice.

I reproduced it twice for BTC, 25 s apart: the drop was 3,112 s, and `openPrice24h` was 77,457.5 against 77,581.7 for the first fill at or after `now − 24h`.

Raw output:
```
sdk {"volume24h":"112430806699788000000000000","baseVolume24h":"144400222000","trades24h":74055,"priceChange24h":"614900000000000000000","high24h":"79550000000000000000000","low24h":"77410800000000000000000","openPrice24h":"77457500000000000000000"}
window SDK folds: [ 1793458800 , 1793542130 ] = 83330 s; trailing 24h is [ 1793455730 , 1793542130 ]; dropped 3070 s
dropped slice: trades 2102 quoteVol 3428448636386000000000000n ...
exact trailing-24h: trades 76157 ... SDK under-reports trades by 2.76% volume by 2.95%
exact open (first fill >= now-24h) 77572500000000000000000 SDK openPrice24h 77457500000000000000000n
```

Suggested fix: either label the window honestly (return `windowStart` and call it "since HH:00 yesterday"), or add the partial head from 60 s candles (or `Fill` rows) between `now − 86400` and the first full hour.

Distinct from known reports: the `statsAsOf`-in-the-future reports (Cubiczan 003, 9xj89gzrtw 02, icohangar 003) and bug-origin's `lastSource.timestamp` report are about the timestamp *label* on the right edge. This report is about missing data at the *left* edge of the window, which changes volume, trade count, open and change.

4.title: Lowercase timeInForce silently selects a GTC limit order
4.original_evidence:
`scripts/r3-sdk-ioc.mjs`, run Sun, 01 Nov 2026 14:11:54 UTC (log: `evidence/r3-sdk-ioc.log`)
```
perp market ETH/USDso:USDso
timeInForce "IOC"  -> orderType 2 (MARKET), returned status "canceled"
timeInForce "ioc"  -> orderType 0 (LIMIT), returned status "open"
timeInForce "Ioc"  -> orderType 0 (LIMIT), returned status "open"
timeInForce "FOK"  -> orderType 1 (FILL_OR_KILL), returned status "canceled"
timeInForce "fok"  -> orderType 0 (LIMIT), returned status "open"
timeInForce "PO"   -> orderType 3 (POST_ONLY), returned status "open"
timeInForce "po"   -> orderType 0 (LIMIT), returned status "open"
timeInForce "GTC"  -> orderType 0 (LIMIT), returned status "open"
```
Suggested fix: `const tif = params.timeInForce?.toUpperCase()`, and throw `InvalidInputError` on anything outside the four values.

Scope: distinct from the `ORDER_TYPE` enum naming item (no `IOC` key) and from the reduceOnly-dropped and market-order IOC override items. This one covers the runtime handling of `CreateOrderParams.timeInForce` values.

```

snapRawToGrid(2.5 ticks, tick, "down")       -> 2000000000000000n
snapRawToGrid(2.5 ticks, tick, "UP")         -> 2000000000000000n
snapRawToGrid(2.5 ticks, tick, "Up")         -> 2000000000000000n

6.original_evidence:
`scripts/r3-sdk-slippage-nan.mjs`, run Sun, 01 Nov 2026 14:12:00 GMT (log: `evidence/r3-sdk-slippage-nan.log`)
```
synthetic mid 100 | 3 base fills at avg 150.33333333333334
fillsWithinSlippage(buy 3, slippage=0.01     ) -> false
fillsWithinSlippage(buy 3, slippage=0.5      ) -> false
fillsWithinSlippage(buy 3, slippage=1        ) -> true
fillsWithinSlippage(buy 3, slippage=NaN      ) -> true
fillsWithinSlippage(buy 3, slippage=undefined) -> true
fillsWithinSlippage(buy 3, slippage=NaN      ) -> true
fillsWithinSlippage(buy 3, slippage=NaN      ) -> true
estimateMarketOrder(buy, NaN)   -> {averagePrice: NaN, baseFilled: NaN, quoteFilled: NaN, levelsConsumed: 0}
estimateMarketOrder(buy, '1')   -> {"averagePrice":101,"baseFilled":1,"quoteFilled":101,"levelsConsumed":1}
live ETH/USDso:USDso: mid 2266.325, 21 ask levels, worst ask 2480, depth 336.6733
  sweeping the whole ask side: avg 2310.644421903964 (1.956% over mid)
  fillsWithinSlippage(buy 336.6733, 0.0001) -> false
  fillsWithinSlippage(buy 336.6733, NaN) -> true
  fillsWithinSlippage(buy 336.6733, undefined) -> true

Suggested fix: `if (!Number.isFinite(slippage) || slippage < 0) throw new InvalidInputError(...)` (or return false), and in `estimateMarketOrder` use `!(amount > 0)` so that NaN returns null.

7.title: Funding helper guards accept windows that cause division by zero
7.original_evidence:
`scripts/r3-sdk-funding-window.mjs`, run Sun, 01 Nov 2026 14:12:03 GMT (log: `evidence/r3-sdk-funding-window.log`)
```
-- window 0.5 s passes assertWindow (positive, finite), then:
annualizedFundingRate(R, 0.5)                        -> 6307.200000000001
intervalsPerWindow(0.5, 0.25)                        -> 2
fundingRate8h(R, 0.5)                                -> THROWS RangeError: Division by zero
fundingRate1h(R, 0.5)                                -> THROWS RangeError: Division by zero
-- window 28800.9 s: siblings disagree (one truncates, one does not)
fundingRate8h(R, 28800.9) * 1095 / 1e18              -> 0.1095
annualizedFundingRate(R, 28800.9)                    -> 0.10949657823193025
-- targetSec / interval not validated at all
normalizeFundingRate(R, 28800, NaN)                  -> THROWS RangeError: The number NaN cannot be converted to a BigInt because it is not an integer
normalizeFundingRate(R, 28800, -3600)                -> -12500000000000n
normalizeFundingRate(R, 28800, 0)                    -> 0n
-- isFundingStale (no validation)
isFundingStale(now-60, NaN, now)                     -> THROWS RangeError: The number NaN cannot be converted to a BigInt because it is not an integer
isFundingStale(now-60, 3601, now, 1.5)               -> THROWS RangeError: The number 5401.5 cannot be converted to a BigInt because it is not an integer
isFundingStale(now-60, -3600, now)                   -> true
isFundingStale(now-60, 0, now)                       -> true
isFundingStale(now-60, 3600, now, 0)                 -> true
intervalsPerWindow(28800, NaN) (contrast: guarded)   -> THROWS RangeError: fundingIntervalSec must be positive, got NaN
```
Source: `dist/funding.js:167-168` (`isFundingStale`, with no guard), `dist/funding.js:280` (`assertWindow`).
Suggested fix: require `Number.isSafeInteger(fundingWindowSec) && fundingWindowSec > 0` in `assertWindow`, apply the same check to `targetSec` and `fundingIntervalSec` in `normalizeFundingRate` and `isFundingStale`, and validate `staleAfterIntervals` as a positive number, computing the threshold before converting to BigInt.

9.title: Backtest CLI silently ignores misspelled top-level flags
9.original_evidence:
- `scripts/backtest.ts:162-196@4e75896`: the loop accepts any `--key` (`flags[key] = val`) with no check against a known-flag list.
- `scripts/backtest.ts:239-241@4e75896`: `takerFeeBps: num("taker-fee-bps", 0)`, `makerFeeBps: num("maker-fee-bps", 0)`, `slippageBps: num("slippage-bps", 0)`: defaults are zero, so a misspelled cost flag yields a no-cost backtest.

20.title: Indexer hooks expose previous-argument data as settled after arguments change
20.original_evidence:
```
{"arg":"0x2a18","q_loading":false,"q_dataFor":"0x2a18","candles_loading":false}
---- rerender with pool B ----
{"arg":"0xdcb0","q_loading":false,"q_dataFor":"0x2a18","candles_loading":false}   <- B requested, A's data, not loading
{"arg":"0xdcb0","q_loading":true,"q_dataFor":"0x2a18","candles_loading":true}     <- still A's data
{"arg":"0xdcb0","q_loading":false,"q_dataFor":"0xdcb0","candles_loading":true}
```
Fix: key the state by deps (store the deps with the result and treat a mismatch as `{ data: undefined, loading: true }` during render), and don't spread old `data` into the loading/error state (or expose it as an explicit `previousData`).
